ss01-xmas.ig:
Christmas budget: start now, not in December.

Split your gift total by the weeks left and set a cap per person before the first purchase. That's the whole trick.

What's your gift budget this year?

Send this to the friend who overspends every December.

#christmasbudget #holidaybudget #savingmoney #budgeting #giftlist
ss01-xmas.tt: Christmas budget: split your gift total by the weeks left, starting now. Set a cap per person before you shop. What's your gift budget this year?
ss01-xmas.src: Weeks counted from late October to December 25.

ss02-packing.ig:
Packing list hack: pack by day, not by item.

Write each day of the trip, pick one outfit per day, then remove the repeats. Less weight, nothing forgotten.

Are you an overpacker or an underpacker?

Send this to the person who always overpacks.

#packinglist #packingtips #traveltips #travelplanning #carryon
ss02-packing.tt: Pack by day, not by item. One outfit per day, then cut the repeats. Overpacker or underpacker?

ss03-zero.ig:
Zero-based budget in one line: give every dollar a job.

Income minus planned spending equals zero. Savings and debt payments count as jobs, so nothing quietly disappears.

Do you know where last month's money went?

Send this to someone who never knows where it went.

#zerobasedbudget #budgeting #moneytips #personalfinance #budgetplanner
ss03-zero.tt: Zero-based budget: every dollar gets a job, savings included. Income minus planned spending equals zero. Do you know where last month's money went?

ss04-buffer.ig:
Travel budget tip: add a 10% buffer line.

Resort fees, tips, transfers, baggage and card fees add up fast. If you don't use the buffer, it pays the next trip's deposit.

What cost surprised you most on your last trip?

Send this to your travel buddy.

#travelbudget #traveltips #tripplanning #budgettravel #travelplanner
ss04-buffer.tt: Add a 10% buffer to every travel budget. Fees and tips always show up. What cost surprised you most on your last trip?

ss05-deposits.ig:
Wedding budget tip: track vendor deposits and balances.

Most vendors take a deposit now and the balance later, on different dates. One list with amount and due date for each vendor keeps you from paying late.

How many vendors are you booking?

Send this to a newly engaged friend.

#weddingbudget #weddingplanning #engaged #weddingvendors #bridetobe
ss05-deposits.tt: Track every wedding vendor deposit and balance with its due date. How many vendors are you booking?

ss06-emergency.ig:
Emergency fund: start with one month, not six.

The usual guideline is three to six months of expenses. Aim for one month of essentials first, then add a little every payday.

How many months do you have right now?

Send this to someone starting from zero.

#emergencyfund #savingmoney #personalfinance #moneytips #budgeting
ss06-emergency.tt: Emergency fund guideline is 3 to 6 months of expenses. Start with one month of essentials. How many months do you have?
ss06-emergency.src: Sources: American Express, How Much Should You Have in an Emergency Fund (americanexpress.com). Fox Business, Emergency fund guidelines.

ss07-venue.ig:
Wedding budget: the venue is usually the biggest line.

The average US reception venue cost $12,900 in 2025, and it also fixes your date and guest count. Price venues first, then build the rest around it.

Venue booked yet?

Send this to someone touring venues this month.

#weddingvenue #weddingbudget #weddingplanning #engaged #weddingplanner
ss07-venue.tt: Average US reception venue in 2025: $12,900. Price venues first. Venue booked yet?
ss07-venue.src: Source: The Knot 2026 Real Weddings Study, couples married in 2025 (theknot.com/content/average-wedding-cost).

ss08-payfirst.ig:
How to save money: save on payday, not at month end.

What's left at the end of the month is usually nothing. Schedule an automatic transfer for the day your pay lands, even 5% to start.

Do you save first or last?

Send this to someone who says they can't save.

#payyourselffirst #savingmoney #moneytips #budgeting #personalfinance
ss08-payfirst.tt: Save on payday with an automatic transfer, not at month end. Start with 5%. Do you save first or last?

ss09-sinking.ig:
Sinking funds: yearly bills without the panic.

A $1,200 yearly bill is $100 a month. Set it aside monthly and the renewal stops being an emergency.

Which yearly bill always catches you off guard?

Send this to someone who dreads renewal season.

#sinkingfunds #budgeting #savingmoney #moneytips #budgetplanner
ss09-sinking.tt: $1,200 a year is $100 a month. Sinking funds turn yearly bills into small monthly ones. Which bill always catches you off guard?

ss10-debt.ig:
Debt snowball vs debt avalanche.

Snowball pays the smallest balance first for quick wins. Avalanche pays the highest interest rate first and usually costs less in interest. The best one is the one you stick to.

Snowball or avalanche?

Send this to someone juggling three credit cards.

#debtfree #debtsnowball #debtavalanche #payoffdebt #personalfinance
ss10-debt.tt: Snowball: smallest balance first. Avalanche: highest rate first, usually less interest. Which one are you?
ss10-debt.src: Sources: Chase, Debt snowball vs avalanche (chase.com). Experian, Avalanche vs snowball (experian.com).

ss11-big3.ig:
Budgeting tip: track housing, transportation and food first.

They make up about 63% of US household spending. Small cuts there move more money than skipping coffee.

Which of the three is your biggest?

Send this to someone tracking every cent.

#budgeting #moneytips #personalfinance #budgetplanner #savingmoney
ss11-big3.tt: Housing, transportation and food are about 63% of US household spending. Start there. Which one is your biggest?
ss11-big3.src: Source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Expenditures 2024: housing 33.4%, transportation 17.0%, food 12.9% (bls.gov).

ss12-fifty.ig:
The 50/30/20 rule starts from take-home pay.

50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings and extra debt payments, all from what actually lands in your account. Popularized by Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi in All Your Worth (2005).

Does your budget start from gross or net?

Send this to the friend who budgets from gross pay.

#503020rule #budgeting #moneytips #personalfinance #budgetplanner
ss12-fifty.tt: 50/30/20 is based on take-home pay, not salary. 50 needs, 30 wants, 20 savings. Gross or net?
ss12-fifty.src: Source: InCharge Debt Solutions, The 50/30/20 Rule (incharge.org), citing All Your Worth, Warren and Warren Tyagi, 2005.

ss13-guests.ig:
Wedding budget: the average works out to about $292 per guest.

The average US wedding in 2025 cost $34,200 for 117 guests. Every guest you cut trims catering, drinks, rentals and favors.

What's your guest count?

Send this to someone writing their guest list.

#weddingbudget #guestlist #weddingplanning #engaged #weddingplanner
ss13-guests.tt: The average US wedding works out to about $292 per guest. What's your guest count?
ss13-guests.src: Source: The Knot 2026 Real Weddings Study, couples married in 2025 (theknot.com/content/average-wedding-cost).

ss14-biweekly.ig:
Biweekly pay: 26 paychecks a year, not 24.

That means most years, two months a year bring a third paycheck. Budget on two per month and send the extras straight to savings or debt.

Do you know your three-paycheck months?

Send this to someone paid every other Friday.

#biweeklybudget #paycheckbudget #budgeting #moneytips #savingmoney
ss14-biweekly.tt: Paid every two weeks? 26 paychecks a year means two months with a third one. Do you know yours?
